findings.issue: When deps.effects is wired (composition root committed to full enforcement per NF-3) but the caller omits invokeCtx entirely, the code defaults declares=[] and the tool is treated as pure-compute, bypassing effect verification. This is distinct from NF-2/AC-8 backward compat (which covers the absent EffectSource port). The spec gives the coder latitude for the 5th-arg absence case (ADR §4.4 option 2: 'no signature break for callers that omit it'), and the in-memory day-1 floor (no Postgres EffectSource DAO until T-0053) means no real enforcement gap exists today. But the comment near line 406 does not articulate the semantic: 'invokeCtx absent + EffectSource present = treats as pure-compute' is an implicit assumption that downstream composition roots should be aware of.
findings.suggestion: Add an inline comment at line 406 clarifying: 'invokeCtx absent means caller asserts no mcp_tool.declares context — treated as pure-compute (empty declares). This is distinct from NF-2 backward compat: EffectSource present + invokeCtx absent still trusts the caller; it is the composition root's responsibility to always supply invokeCtx when invoking an mcp_tool handle.' This documents the trust boundary without breaking the interface.
